title: Insurance Claim Repairs Cashier Standard — Payment Against Which an Overpayment Is Refunded
content:
An overpayment refund on an Insurance Claim Repairs repair order is returned against one customer payment on the repair order and is never more than that payment. The payment refunded follows the payment methods on the repair order:

1. **the most recent card payment**, when a card payment was made no more than the card refund window of **120 days** before today;
2. otherwise **the most recent ACH payment**, when one was made at least the ACH return days of **5 days** before today;
3. otherwise **the most recent customer payment**, by any method.

Days are calendar days from the payment's entry date to today. The refund goes back to the method of the payment chosen and is capped at that payment's amount.

## Method table

| Most recent card payment | Most recent ACH payment | Payment refunded and cap |
|---|---|---|
| made 120 days or fewer before today | any | that card payment |
| made more than 120 days before today, or no card payment | made 5 days or more before today | that ACH payment |
| made more than 120 days before today, or no card payment | made fewer than 5 days before today, or no ACH payment | the most recent customer payment of any method |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical payment histories)

- Most recent card payment 120 days ago: within the window — refunded against that card payment.
- Most recent card payment 121 days ago and an ACH payment 5 days ago: the ACH payment.
- Most recent card payment 121 days ago and an ACH payment 4 days ago: neither qualifies — the most recent customer payment, which here is that ACH payment, being the latest of all.
- Only a cash payment of USD 300.00 and a check payment of USD 200.00 made after it: the most recent customer payment, the USD 200.00 check, and the refund is at most USD 200.00.
